results.evidence:
InviteModal.tsx InviteRow: `status={rowValidation?.error ? 'danger' : 'default'}` on the LemonInput and `{rowValidation?.error ? (
) : null}` render inline error styling and message on the row itself. `rowValidation` comes from `inviteRowValidations[index]`, computed client-side from `membersLogic.selectors.members` in inviteLogic.ts, so it fires before any submit action.

`validateInviteRow` in inviteLogic.ts: `if (ownEmail && normalized === normalizeInviteEmail(ownEmail)) { return { isValid: false, error: SELF_INVITE_ERROR } }` runs the same normalization/flagging path as the existing-member check, sourcing `ownEmail` from `userLogic.selectors.user`.

InviteModal.tsx submit button: `disabledReason={... !canSubmit ? (rowError ?? 'Please fill out all fields') : undefined}` where `rowError` is the row validation error text (e.g. "...Remove this email or invite someone else.") and `canSubmit` requires `validations.every((validation) => validation.isValid)`. OnboardingInviteTeammates.tsx uses the same `inviteRowValidations`/`canSubmitInvites` via the shared `inviteLogic` and shared `InviteTeamMatesComponent`, with `continueDisabledReason` set to `rowError ?? 'Please enter a valid email address'`. Per-row: `disabled={!rowValidation?.isValid || !invitesToSend[index].target_email}` on the per-row submit button in InviteRow.

`normalizeInviteEmail` does `email.trim().replace(/[A-Z]/g, (letter) => String.fromCharCode(letter.charCodeAt(0) + 32))`, and `memberEmailSet` applies this same normalization to `member.user.email` before insertion into the set used for comparison, so case and whitespace differences are ignored on both sides.

`InviteTeamMatesComponent` (shared by both the settings dialog and onboarding step) calls `useOnMountEffect(ensureAllMembersLoaded)` via `membersLogic`. The own-email branch in `validateInviteRow` is checked unconditionally before the `memberEmails.has(normalized)` branch, so it applies regardless of whether members have loaded.

The membership check moved from `create()` into `validate_target_email`, run during `is_valid()`: `if OrganizationMembership.objects.filter(...).exists(): raise exceptions.ValidationError(..., code="already_member")`. The accompanying comment states the intent explicitly: "A membership hit has to fail here, during is_valid(), or earlier rows in the same request are already sent." Since DRF's bulk `is_valid()` validates all rows before any `.save()`/`create()` is invoked, a failing row anywhere prevents `create()` (and thus `send_invite`) from running for any row in the batch.

`validate_target_email` (a DRF field-level validator, so its error is attributed to `target_email`) raises `exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="already_member")`, and the frontend defines the matching constant `ALREADY_MEMBER_INVITE_ERROR_CODE = 'already_member'` with a comment noting it must stay in sync with this backend code.

`shouldReportApiFailure` now includes: `if (status === 400 && failure.code === ALREADY_MEMBER_INVITE_ERROR_CODE) { return false }`, alongside the existing doc listing other genuinely-unexpected failures (plain 500s, status-less TypeErrors, etc.) that remain reportable, so only this specific validation outcome is excluded from error tracking on the same generic API failure path.

The only listeners shown in inviteLogic.ts are `inviteTeamMembersSuccess` (which reloads org/invites) and `addProjectAccess`; there is no `inviteTeamMembersFailure` listener or any other code path that reloads `membersLogic` members when the server rejects a submission with an already_member error the client didn't flag beforehand.

result:
Inviting an email that already belongs to the organization (including your own) is now caught on the invite row, and a batch that includes one is rejected before any invite is created or emailed. That rejection is no longer reported as an application error.

The settings invite dialog and the onboarding invite step share the same rows. Those rows only checked that an address looked like an email, so an existing member was discovered after submit, as a generic error toast. On the server, the membership check ran inside `create()`, after `is_valid()` had passed. Bulk save creates one row at a time and sends the email inside that create, so earlier rows in the same request were already emailed when a later row failed. The resulting 400 was then filed by the frontend error reporter, which treats ordinary 400s as unexpected.

`OrganizationInviteSerializer.validate_target_email` now rejects an address that matches an organization member, with code `already_member`, before any row is saved. Single and bulk invites both go through that validation, so a batch fails up front and sends nothing. The frontend loads organization members when the invite form mounts and marks a row invalid when the address is yours or another member's, including case differences. Submit stays disabled, and the row says to remove that email or invite someone else. `shouldReportApiFailure` ignores 400s with code `already_member`, so a request that still hits the API is not filed as an application error.

Tests cover the row flag (your own email before the member list loads, and a later row blocking the rest of the batch) and the API (case-insensitive single invite, plus a bulk request whose third address is an existing member or yourself: 400, no invites, no emails, and no exception capture).
